correctness.rationale: For self-adjoint 0<=F<=qI, the centered operator F-qI/2 has norm <=q/2. Therefore H u=(q/2)u+(F-qI/2)Pu+(G-qI/2)(I-P)u gives ||Hu||<=q/2+(q/2)(||Pu||+||(I-P)u||)<=q(1+sqrt(2))/2 for every dimension. In dimension 2, P=diag(1,0) and rank-one F,G projectors onto symmetric vectors at angle pi/8 produce a symmetric H with norm exactly C=(1+sqrt(2))/2. Scaling and small positive-definite perturbation establish iff damping threshold qcrit=2/(1+sqrt(2)). The supplied same-generator backward-Euler example A=diag(1/2000,5), F=(I+A/2)^(-2), G=(I+A)^(-1), P=ones(2,2)/2 has exact ||H e1||^2-1=31863808011974591697209/39416723919275164992358416>0 (independently rederived using rational arithmetic), while G-F is positive diagonal and H is similar via positive diagonal scaling to G-(G-F)^(1/2)P(G-F)^(1/2), Hermitian lying strictly between F and G: spectrum inside (0,1). This is transient one-step growth, not divergence.
